Usage

Gross-Boult volume-corrected residual: mean( (sqrt(a1 a2 a3)(F^eps1 - 1))^2 ).

inside_outside(points, a, eps, R, t) gives the inside-outside function F of each point, and the mean square of the per-point residual r_i = sqrt(a1*a2*a3) * (F_i**eps1 - 1) is returned as a float. A point on the surface has F=1, so its residual is 0; inside points get a negative and outside points a positive residual (squaring removes the sign). It is the same quantity that fit_superquadric minimises, and the residual of the returned dict is this value too.

• points: a point cloud that can be reshaped to (N,3) (world coordinates).

• a: radii (a1,a2,a3). eps: shape exponents (eps1,eps2) (computing F uses both; the outer F**eps1 uses eps1 only).

• R/t: pose (X_body = R.T @ (X - t)). None means identity rotation / origin.

Numerical guard: F is clipped to [0, 1e12], and a1*a2*a3 is raised to at least 1e-12 before the sqrt is taken (so that degenerate parameters do not give inf/NaN; values near the surface are unaffected).

Dimensions: sqrt(a1 a2 a3) is length to the power 3/2 and F^eps1 - 1 is dimensionless, so the return value has the dimension of length to the power 3 and depends on the scale of the point cloud. It is not suited to comparing objects of different sizes. That it is a radial-distance approximation rather than the true point-to-surface Euclidean distance, and that it has no protection against outliers, are as described in the module docstring.

The 3d op superquadric_residual bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tunable parameters; neither a nor b is used.
